commands.command: Schema-compatibility audit before adding any new closed-enum vocabulary
commands.summary: A focused test (durable::tests::a_nested_closed_enum_field_carries_the_identical_hazard_as_a_top_level_kind) proves a nested closed enum field (symbol_kind-shaped -- the exact shape a new manifest_kind field would have) carries the identical old-reader-hard-fails hazard as a top-level GraphNodeKind/GraphEdgeKind addition. Conclusion: schema v3 genuinely necessary for this checkpoint's new ManifestKind/SourceLanguage vocabulary. Decision 0048 records the audit and authorizes the bump; CURRENT_GRAPH_SCHEMA_VERSION -> 3, SUPPORTED_GRAPH_SCHEMA_VERSIONS -> [1,2,3]. Two new tests (a_genuine_v2_semantic_graph_remains_readable_and_valid, a_v2_graph_rebuilds_deterministically_into_a_valid_v3_graph) mirror the existing v1 compatibility proofs one major up.

126/126 total (83 pre-existing at this checkpoint's start + 43 new: 1 nested-enum schema-hazard audit test, 8 metadata-adapter policy/heuristic tests, 16 TOML/JSON/YAML/Markdown adapter tests, 2 v2/v3 schema compatibility tests, 2 Rust Exports tests, 5 ROG-021 graph-level boundary tests, 8 metadata incremental-equivalence tests, 1 metadata overlay test).
Full workspace green (repopact-graph 126, repopact-desktop-api 14 unaffected, repopact-validation 49, repopact-mutation 15, all others unaffected).

Four MetadataAdapter implementations: TOML (Cargo.toml package/workspace-members/dependencies/dev-dependencies/build-dependencies/workspace.dependencies; pyproject.toml project identity/dependencies/optional-dependency-groups/scripts/build-backend), JSON (package.json identity/dependencies/devDependencies/peerDependencies/scripts; tsconfig*.json extends/references/select compilerOptions), YAML (a deterministic line-oriented indentation-aware scanner for .github/workflows/*.yml -- workflow name/jobs/uses/run/working-directory; ${{ ... }} expressions recorded symbolically, never evaluated), Markdown (heading hierarchy, repository-relative links excluding external URLs/anchors, code-fence languages, front-matter presence -- structural only, no prose bodies stored, bounded to 500 facts/document). An unrecognized file within a supported metadata language is explicitly skipped (SkipReason::UnrecognizedMetadataSchema), never fabricated into facts. Dependency/reference targets are local fact nodes, never edges resolved into another file's own manifest node (no cross-file lookup performed, consistent with Decision 0045's 'import fact, not resolved target' precedent).

Bare-pub modules/functions/structs/enums/traits/type-aliases now emit the already-declared (Decision 0045) GraphEdgeKind::Exports edge; pub(crate)/pub(super)/private items and #[test] functions never do. 2 new focused tests. Implements/Extends/References/Calls/UsesType remain declared-but-unemitted -- no false resolver introduced this checkpoint.

metadata::policy adds deterministic, centralized minified-content (size + newline-density heuristic) and generated-content (bounded marker scan) classification, applied uniformly ahead of every adapter (source and metadata alike) via two new SkipReason variants. 8 boundary tests including explicit false-positive guards (ordinary prose mentioning 'generate', a marker outside the bounded scan window, a short one-liner).

A near-limit fixture (three ~2,000-line/~100KB Rust/Python/TypeScript files, plus a pathological single-line deeply-nested Rust file) was built via the real engine binary on native Windows, measuring actual PeakWorkingSet64 via the OS process handle (not a pipe-based measurement, which deadlocked on first attempt and was corrected to file-redirected I/O). Result: 16.27 MB peak working set for the full build (6,009 nodes, 8,008 edges). The pathological nested file was caught by the minified-content policy (a single ~16KB line, near-zero newline density) before ever reaching the parser -- a real, measured instance of defense-in-depth, not merely a unit-tested code path in isolation. This is engineering measurement, not a claimed hard memory cap -- the honest contract remains bounded input size + parser timeout/cancellation + this measured (not guessed) peak-memory data point.

5 new tests build a real graph and inspect its actual nodes/edges (not the underlying repopact-repository walker's own separately-tested logic): excluded target/node_modules/.venv trees produce zero graph nodes; .git internals (including a nested repository's own .git) are never indexed as source; a nested repository is classified GraphNodeKind::NestedRepository while its internals stay bounded; a .env-shaped file is still truthfully listed as a physical fact (a content digest) but its actual secret value never appears as any node label; a symlink pointing outside the repository is not traversed -- content reachable only through it never appears in the graph (symlink creation succeeded on this Windows machine, not merely skipped).

8 new tests prove byte-for-byte equivalence between an incremental graph.update and a clean full rebuild for: Cargo.toml dependency and workspace-member changes, pyproject.toml dependency changes, package.json script changes, tsconfig.json reference changes, a CI workflow job change, and a Markdown link change -- plus a dedicated test confirming a metadata-only edit reparses exactly the one manifest file, never the unrelated Rust/Python/TypeScript source files in the same fixture. This work incidentally caught and fixed a genuine pre-existing bug: incremental::read_semantic_contributions_by_file filtered reusable prior contributions by layer==Semantic only, silently dropping every metadata fact (layer Package/Build) on an unchanged-file classification during incremental reconciliation while a clean full rebuild always regenerated them correctly -- corrected to filter by 'not Governance/Physical' so every current and future contribution layer is reusable.

1 new test proves a Cargo.toml dependency edit through SessionGraphState::reconcile updates the in-memory graph, regenerates only that file's own contribution, reuses unrelated source contributions untouched, discloses basis=working_overlay, and never writes rog/ (hashed before/after).

Metadata adapter identities/versions merge into the existing SemanticCompatibility.adapter_versions map (one map, not a second field, since a version change in either family invalidates reuse identically); CURRENT_RESOURCE_POLICY_VERSION bumped to resource-policy-2 since the new minified/generated policy checks change what the same bytes produce -- a durable baseline written before this checkpoint is correctly treated as incompatible for semantic reuse and falls back to a full rebuild.

commands.command: Coverage-disclosure bug found and fixed during real self-build inspection
commands.summary: aggregate_coverage's adapter_versions/relations_supported (the durable manifest's own coverage record, distinct from the reuse-compatibility identity above) only ever included the three source-language adapters -- discovered because a real RepoPact self-build processed 424 metadata files but the manifest gave no indication any metadata adapter had run. Fixed by merging metadata::adapter_versions()/relations_supported() into the same disclosed map.

An 11-file fixture (Rust with a module/test, Python, TypeScript, Cargo.toml with a dependency, pyproject.toml with a script entrypoint, package.json with a dependency/script, tsconfig.json with extends, a CI workflow YAML, a Markdown document with headings/links/a fence, an unrecognized generic JSON file, and a malformed Rust file), confirmed byte-identical by SHA-256 of every source file, was built independently on native Windows (two consecutive builds, byte-identical rog/ directories confirming same-platform determinism) and a freshly re-synced Linux-native WSL2 Debian 13 checkout (~/repopact-linux, never /mnt/c/...). Result: identical fingerprint (0e565977854c2cbaff84b2bd1bd6328103d25e64265483dd122af4bc3356685e), node_count 43, edge_count 52, identical semantic_coverage (11 considered/9 complete/1 partial/0 failed/0 unsupported-language/1 policy-skipped), and all 32 manifest+shard SHA-256 hashes byte-identical between platforms. No macOS execution occurred or is claimed.
